sentence: This project builds computational methods that analyze cancer genomes to find alterations that help cancer develop or bring about an anti-tumor immune response.
This project studies how chondrocytes in growth plates swell and how these swollen cells secrete the mineralized scaffold of bone.
This project tests whether machine learning can use neuropsychological test results and clock drawing videos to detect Alzheimer’s disease in Veterans.
This project studies whether amyloid beta neuropathology and sepsis increase activity of the complement system in the brain, causing neuroinflammation and synapse loss.
This project studies how the complement pathway reprograms macrophages and promotes liver cancer in a form of fatty liver disease.
This project builds a continuous apnea monitor that can better describe apnea of prematurity in premature newborns.
This project measures how differences in genome sequence affect proteins in yeast and builds models that predict their effects on health.
This project studies how chromosomal instability helps non-small cell lung cancer evade the immune system and cause brain metastasis.
This project studies how early-life exposures relate to dysanapsis, a mismatch between airway tree and lung size, throughout childhood and adolescence.
This project studies how daily rhythms affect tissue regrowth and builds robotic and drug delivery tools to control those rhythms.
This project studies the mechanism behind damage to the lining of blood vessels caused by blood loss in trauma.
This project uses multiomic profiling to find subclasses of early-life immune development linked to vaccine response, respiratory infection and asthma in children.
This project builds a data analysis platform that combines clinical, genomics and proteomics data from tumors to study cancer biology and drug resistance.
This project studies how risk and protective factors from peer, family and school change across adolescence and relate to substance use in youth.
This project provides a genetic material repository, a genetic database and analysis support to help study how genes relate to dementia.
This project builds high-speed microscopy and voltage indicators that image the electrical activity of large neuronal populations deep in tissue.
This project sequences whole genomes from people of African, European and Native Brazilian ancestry to find links with clinical and neuropathologic traits.
This project builds computational tools that use DNA and RNA sequencing to find and describe structural variants in a large population of samples.
This project tests in mice whether lipid nanoparticles can deliver a gene into melanoma cells that makes them targets for destruction.
This project designs sensor molecules that show where and how ubiquitin attaches to histone proteins in the cell nucleus.
